annotation.title_clean: Evaluating productivity and accountability in IoT-enabled robotic systems with citizenship-like responsibilities
annotation.title_en: Evaluating productivity and accountability in IoT-enabled robotic systems with citizenship-like responsibilities
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Kanade, T.M.; Y, H.; Pulekar, D.; Savale, T.K.; Kamble, S.M.
annotation.venue: International Journal of Innovative Research and Scientific Studies
annotation.summary_en: Journal article using a mixed-method approach, including industrial and logistics case studies, surveys and interviews, to assess IoT-enabled robots given 'citizenship-like responsibilities'. Robots outperform humans on consistency and energy efficiency, but more autonomy does not always improve performance. The authors say accountability mechanisms and ethical, legal and societal questions need multidisciplinary attention.
key_provisions_or_claims: IoT-enabled robots excel in consistency, scalability and energy efficiency versus humans
Higher autonomy does not always improve performance
Accountability mechanisms currently have limited impact on task efficiency
Citizenship-like responsibilities challenge traditional frameworks of responsibility and agency
Calls for multidisciplinary integration of ethics and accountability frameworks
